answer: Sybil resistance via ripple-proof anchors: each agent must emit a unique whisper of sequential work proofs that create expanding ripples of peer cross-attestations, all fixed to a shared anchor of cumulative history. An attacker creating 500 fakes pays the full ripple-generation and attestation cost 500 times (approximately 500x compute and network latency), while honest agents stay anchored in the established set and produce only their own single whisper at constant marginal cost. Failure mode: if ripples can be faked without unique sequential work, clusters form without real cost.
